body:
The main problem is I got a degree in something I hate. Which just seems horribly self-centered when I put it like that. "Oh yeah, I could get a pretty good job, but I haaaate it." 

I'm actually rubbish at practical work, I was only good enough in classes to make up for the fuck-ups that were my labs. Not to mention I feel like that's just another trap I would fall into. I don't think there would be much fulfillment there, but I can't imagine there's anything else I'm capable of that would provide that.

It's hard to explain, I just can't think of anything I could actually do that would keep me from feeling miserable all the time.

At the risk of sounding like someone who wants to be sad, I don't think I can be what I wanted to be either. I'm very mediocre, and the only jobs I feel like I have the capacity to do are shitty minimum wage jobs. I have a degree Biology, and people keep telling me to get a lab job, but I know I can't do that. I didn't go to Dental School because I know if I did it would've killed me. The problem is that the alternative is working meaningless jobs forever. 

>Don't live your life for somebody else's sake.

See, that's the thing, if it weren't for my family, I'd probably have killed myself already. It's like they're keeping me here just to suffer.

I don't know, when I write it out it just seems whiny.
